author: josh1125
text:
This is the way I see it. We have Flags, FTRs then the FL. A flag is
just a stop in momentum after an important area is broken. Our FTR is
when an important area is broken, then price stops in momentum the
continues in the direction of the engulf. Now our Flag Limit (FL) is
present in both the FTR and the Flag. The FL is simply exactly what its
name say it is; it's our Flag Limit. Price consolidates between the
limits. I've added a chart to show exactly what I'm saying. If I'm wrong
 on this matter, please correct me, because this subject is a very
important piece of the puzzle.

author: changbachang
text:
charlespips wrote: Guys,

FL is the two lines/zones that 'enclose' the flag area like a sandwich.
The bread is the limit, Not the egg inside. I remember that we must find
 setup on the edge, which in this case the 'Flag Limit' itself, not
inside the flag. The edge where the price break later become the new DP
point for price to return to. So I guess we must look at the limit, not
the flag area itself (which is mid range).

As for FTRs vs FLs, It's the same thing guys. what's become important is
 that not all FTR/FL is good for entry. It MUST break important key
levels before you can consider its value. That's my half cent.

Please kindly correct me if I'm wrong.

text:
Chang you need to understand and study what is being taught here. I
can tell by your posts that you are at the beginning of your studies.
Switching markets, won't really help you long term. You will have to
dig for many 100's of hours on each subject and then integrate it all
together. From what I see in your journal you're looking for patterns
and engulfs which will tell you price is changing direction. This is
only a small piece of the puzzle. If we simply trade QMs, engulfs etc
at HTF S/D we will only be pattern traders and we might as well slap
MACD and moon cycles back on our charts. We have to know where price
can overshoot and under shoot too and then if we are prepared to trade
in those areas. This takes experience which you can't get by studying
for a few months.

Don't allow yourself the luxury of making excuses that forex or any
other market is too manipulated for your to succeed. IF, Kruger, Harry,
 Gil and many of the bright shining stars on here do it day in day out.
 We have to be tough on ourselves and study hard trusting that if they
can do it so can we. Cheers.

author: smimon
text:
Just to add my two cents. I only found RTM at the end of September.
For the first month, I was trying to "predict" what was going to happen,
 by analysing the charts down to the finest detail, and simple to say, I
 failed miserably, due to lack of experience in such things.

But does that mean I can't trade, and trade very successfully with the things taught on here? No, not at all.

My biggest strides forward came when I gave up trying to predict what
was going to happen, and just let the market show me its intentions.
Think you've spotted a level that price is going to turn at? Great, now
wait and see what happens. Got a significant engulf off the level you
want? Check again - was it really significant? Or has it just come down
to a SR flip level to continue in the way it was already going? How is
price moving? Has it shot up to your level with a single big candle? Has
 it compressed towards it? Has it proceeded up in a series of surges,
forming fresh demand levels every step of the way?

All we need to trade successfully is the ability to spot potential
turning points ahead of time, and then just wait and see what happens
when we get there. If we see things lining up in our favour, take the
trade, and set your target at the first point you can realistically
expect trouble from. Don't "expect" price to blow through several levels
 of strong supply or demand to some hollywood target.

There are plenty of pips out there, if one would just be patient, and let the market tell us what it wants to do.

Predicting huge moves, and setting POs ahead of time with pinpoint
accuracy is something I'm sure I will be able to do with 100s more hours
 of chart time, but right now, I've got more than enough tools in my kit
 with the things that are taught on here to be profitable.
